+    def _is_all_or_any_call(self, call):
+        """Check if a call is to all() or any() with a generator expression or list comprehension."""
+        if not isinstance(call, ast.Call):
+            return False, None, None
+        
+        if not isinstance(call.func, ast.Name):
+            return False, None, None
+        
+        if call.func.id not in ('all', 'any'):
+            return False, None, None
+        
+        if len(call.args) != 1 or call.keywords:
+            return False, None, None
+        
+        arg = call.args[0]
+        if isinstance(arg, (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp)):
+            return True, call.func.id, arg
+        
+        return False, None, None
+
+    def _handle_all_or_any_call(self, call, assert_):
+        """Handle all() and any() calls by unrolling them into for loops with asserts."""
+        is_all_any, func_name, iterable_node = self._is_all_or_any_call(call)
+        
+        if not is_all_any:
+            return None
+        
+        # Get the first (and usually only) comprehension
+        comp = iterable_node.generators[0]
+        
+        # For all(): assert each element
+        # For any(): we need to check if at least one element is truthy
+        
+        # Create the assertion for the element
+        element_assert = ast.Assert(
+            test=iterable_node.elt,
+            msg=None,
+            lineno=assert_.lineno,
+            col_offset=assert_.col_offset
+        )
+        
+        # Create the for loop
+        for_loop = ast.For(
+            target=comp.target,
+            iter=comp.iter,
+            body=[element_assert],
+            orelse=[],
+            lineno=assert_.lineno,
+            col_offset=assert_.col_offset
+        )
+        
+        return [for_loop]
